excerpt: Moveworks makes an AI assistant that lets employees get IT, HR and other requests resolved in chat. Founded in 2016, it was acquired by ServiceNow in December 2025.
content:
Moveworks builds an AI assistant for employees inside large companies. Instead of filing a ticket and waiting, a worker can ask the assistant in chat to reset a password, request software access, find a policy or update personal details, and it searches company knowledge and takes the action in the underlying business systems where it can. Moveworks describes it as an AI assistant platform for the entire workforce to search and act across business applications, built on what it calls a reasoning engine plus enterprise search. Entrepreneur India reported that close to 90% of its customers have rolled the assistant out to their whole workforce.

Moveworks was founded in 2016 by Bhavin Shah (CEO), Varun Singh (president), Jiang Chen and Vaibhav Nivargi, according to its about page. It is headquartered in Mountain View, California, with offices in San Francisco, Austin, New York and Bangalore. The same page says it raised $315 million at a $2.1 billion valuation and lists customers such as Toyota, Instacart, CVS Health, Marriott, HP, GitHub, Databricks and Micron. In December 2025 Moveworks said it served more than 350 enterprise customers and 5.5 million employees.

Moveworks is now part of ServiceNow. ServiceNow announced on 15 December 2025 that it had completed the acquisition, which Moveworks' own post called the largest in ServiceNow's history. The two companies had partnered for eight years and shared about 250 customers. ServiceNow said the combination pairs its agentic AI and workflow automation with Moveworks' assistant, enterprise search and reasoning technology to create an AI front door for work. Moveworks said standalone customers keep the full assistant, while ServiceNow customers get tighter integration across IT, HR and other services. The price was not disclosed in the announcements we read.

Moveworks does not publish prices; enterprise contracts are quoted after a demo.

This page is research, not a review. We have not used Moveworks; facts come from its pages and the reporting under Sources.
